humanAcceptance.evidence: After the immutable Pass 64 preview existed, Codex applied Dave's standing instruction in the active task: once all requested work is implemented, push Pass 64 as Live and keep Pass 63 as Stable. This records that conditional release authorization against the exact completed runtime SHA.

requirements.summary: Complete playable hardware WebGPU and TSL migration
requirements.expected: The normal Pass 64 game runs gameplay, physics, bots, multiplayer, HUD and all arenas on an actual fail-closed WebGPU backend with TSL pipelines, selected-only arena residency and one controlled HDR path; WebGL2 remains explicit compatibility only.
requirements.falsifier: The required route falls back, loads a legacy shader, loses the device, retains multiple arena roots, misses a TSL/HDR identity, or omits playable game systems.

evidence.note: Exact clean SHA c30fb9a passed actual NVIDIA WebGPU identity, four-arena switching, TSL traversal, HDR samples, zero device loss, single-root streaming, light occlusion and performance budgets.
Proves fail-closed CI behavior, WebGL compatibility telemetry and the served Terminal renderer foundation.
Exact-SHA hardware captures cover the complete playable route across all four arenas.

requirements.summary: Terminal world-loss, roof, opening and lighting integrity
requirements.expected: Terminal retains its drawable selected world while HUD and atmosphere run, exposes a real aircraft ceiling and valid open boarding route, and keeps practical light behind opaque geometry.
requirements.falsifier: The world collapses to a flat fog colour, a stable selected root is detached/hidden/empty, the cabin roof disappears, an open route blocks, or a local light leaks through a closed wall.

evidence.note: The watchdog excludes only the atomic switch transaction, repairs only the exact adopted root, and marks stable missing geometry fatal rather than masking it.
Deterministic served capture covers the Terminal cabin ceiling and boarding opening.
The served Terminal cabin/roof/opening test passes and asserts a healthy non-fatal selected-world watchdog.

requirements.summary: Bright modern behavior-complete HUD and menu overhaul
requirements.expected: Setup, lobby, loadout, gameplay, death, match-end and returned-lobby states use a bright readable tactical composition with no critical overlaps or tiny unreadable text while retaining every gameplay and accessibility surface.
requirements.falsifier: A required control disappears, map or damage surfaces overlap, critical text falls below the contract, focus escapes, narrow/ultrawide layouts clip, or the interface regresses to the rejected dark-blue composition.

evidence.note: All 13 HUD tests pass across laptop, desktop, ultrawide, narrow, high-DPI, live, dead, match-end and returned-lobby states with overlap and font-size assertions.
The refreshed review corpus contains real world frames and the new command composition at every required viewport.

requirements.expected: Nuke Town, Terminal and RustRig show renderer-backed helicopter flyovers, while Gun Range uses the cat's first-person view; motion is smooth, deterministic for review and static under reduced-motion preference.
requirements.falsifier: A map shows a static poster only, the wrong framing is selected, movement stalls, the gameplay camera is mutated after deployment, or reduced-motion hides information.

evidence.note: Typed poses cover every canonical arena and deterministic/reduced-motion behavior.

evidence.command: npx playwright test tests/e2e/pass64-hud-menu.spec.ts --project=chromium --workers=1 --grep "animates the live arena preview"
evidence.note: The served renderer canvas moves through a real preview pose and stays inside the intended showcase.
The exact-SHA viewport corpus shows the helo and cat frames in the redesigned selector.

requirements.summary: Repeatable lobby, rematch and close-tab recovery
requirements.expected: Host and guests return to one pure waiting lobby, all can ready again, a second match starts, and a reconnecting tab recovers the intended identity without cloning live data channels.
requirements.falsifier: Either match clock remains populated, readiness diverges, match two cannot start, signalling loss destroys healthy channels, or two tabs claim one guest identity.

evidence.note: Two cycles with one host and two guests clear both clocks and all readiness flags, ready everyone again, start match two, and observe leave/rejoin grace.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/room-rejoin-identity.test.ts src/network-lifecycle.test.ts src/private-match.test.ts
evidence.note: Covers per-tab ownership leases, 90-second recovery identity and signalling/data-channel lifecycle.

requirements.summary: Shot timing, health regeneration and Free For All spawn correctness
requirements.expected: Authoritative shot timing remains exact under impairment, regenerated remote health survives a later small hit, early FFA protection is symmetric, and initial peers reserve distinct authored spawns at least eight metres apart when the map supports it.
requirements.falsifier: Host and guest disagree, valid shots are universally blocked at match start, a healed player dies to a small hit, one peer retains asymmetric immunity, or simultaneous initial peers choose the same spawn.

evidence.note: Impaired two-peer run accepted and confirmed 7 of 7 shots with exact agreement and no rewind rejection or event-lane pressure.
Both cycles recovered remote health to about 99 HP and survived the next 10-damage hit at about 89 HP.
Deterministic locale-independent roster reservations prove separated initial spawns and explicit bounded fallback.

requirements.summary: Host-authoritative railgun with high-impact shared presentation
requirements.expected: The eight-round Nuke Town railgun spawns after three minutes, announces once, penetrates the map for 50 damage, forces ADS exit and a 1.5-second rechamber, never replenishes, shows high-refresh blue hostile silhouettes through walls, and emits a massive shared beam and audible report.
requirements.falsifier: Spawn/pickup/damage/ammo diverges, a repeat shot fires early, thermal shows invalid contacts, a remote shot lacks the beam/report, or ammo replenishes.

evidence.note: Served gameplay proves ADS exit, exact rechamber, second-shot admission and presentation telemetry.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/railgun-authority.test.ts src/railgun-presentation.test.ts src/audio-railgun.test.ts
evidence.note: Covers authority, pooled local/replicated beam, 3D thermal silhouettes and the bounded eight-layer local/remote report.
Exact-SHA browser evidence contains the shared beam and thermal presentation.

requirements.summary: RustRig ocean, materials, mist, lights and z-fight quality
requirements.expected: RustRig retains its authored routes and assets while gaining coherent industrial textures, large layered waves, light-reactive mist and purposeful warm practicals without coplanar deck flicker or pitch-black play lanes.
requirements.falsifier: Deck surfaces z-fight, the sea is flat/static, mist ignores the lighting profile, practicals leak or exceed budget, routes change, or representative lanes are unreadably dark.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/additional-maps.test.ts src/arena-contrast-lighting.test.ts src/rendering/pass64-tsl-scene.test.ts
evidence.note: Covers deterministic material families, animated warm lighting, three-band TSL water and mist policy.
Hardware review and budget receipt include RustRig wave, mist, warm-light and single-root presentation.
The exact hardware capture records the revised RustRig composition.

requirements.summary: Gun Range lighting and moving targets plus global combat readability
requirements.expected: Gun Range has animated lit targets and shooting-bay lighting; bots are half as emissive across arenas; decals respect material families; and tracers are subtly bolder and longer-lived without changing hit authority.
requirements.falsifier: Targets remain static/unlit, bays are unreadable, bots retain the overbright profile, impact marks ignore materials, or tracer/impact pools cause unbounded growth.

evidence.command: npx vitest run src/additional-maps.test.ts src/operator-model.test.ts src/impact-presentation.test.ts
evidence.note: Covers moving target lights, bay motion, global 0.5 emissive multiplier and material-specific pooled decals.
Gun Range passes actual WebGPU lighting, shadow and frame budgets.
The exact hardware capture records the animated target and bay-light environment.

requirements.summary: Retained gameplay, chat, grenade, killstreak, class and canonical operator contracts
requirements.expected: Chat fades and reopens in lobby/match; normal grenades beep and explode conventionally; Terminal supports killstreaks and damage; class redeploy has no fake death; 2x Damage avoids spawn hitch; and players, bots and corpses use the canonical rigged operator family.
requirements.falsifier: Any listed behavior regresses, the 2x spawn stalls peers, a class switch records combat side effects, or a block-built runtime body returns.

evidence.note: The complete 763-test suite retains room chat, grenade audio/model, support, killstreak, redeploy, prewarm, canonical corpse/operator, lobby and arena contracts.
Real peers prove clean redeploy and replicated railgun/drop state across the retained lifecycle.

requirements.summary: Lightweight post-match diagnostics and log analysis
requirements.expected: Combat/health/timing evidence is bounded in memory during play and uploaded only post-match through a private validated idempotent envelope, never over gameplay channels and never with chat, room codes, raw peer IDs, IPs or credentials.
requirements.falsifier: Diagnostics add active-match traffic, exceed caps, retain prohibited data, clear an unacknowledged queue, expose public reads, or fail schema/idempotency checks.

evidence.note: A completed match emits one private envelope after play with zero active-match diagnostic requests.
All 41 diagnostics schema, uploader, analyzer, collector and Worker validation tests pass.

requirements.summary: Pass 64 Live with byte-exact Pass 63 Stable and retained Pass 62 benchmark
requirements.expected: The chooser exposes only Pass 64 Live and Pass 63 Stable, aliases enter Pass 64, Pass 63 is copied byte-exact from production source 1bd55076 and Pages 2201a606, and the immutable Pass 62 best-netcode benchmark remains verifiable separately.
requirements.falsifier: Pass 63 is rebuilt, a pinned byte/digest differs, an alias enters the wrong channel, an extra channel appears, or the Pass 62 benchmark record is overwritten or reclassified.

evidence.command: npm run build && npm run stage:release-topology && npm run verify:release-topology
evidence.note: Stages and byte-compares the 120-file complete Pass 63 Pages subtree against the pinned production commit while preserving its 119-file runtime digest.
Pass 62 remains an independent immutable 118-file benchmark with digest 035e868a while Pass 63 is current Stable.

requirements.summary: Exact immutable Pass 64 candidate is authorized for production
requirements.expected: The published runtime derives from exact preview source c30fb9a and differs afterward only by this acceptance manifest and allowed process metadata; protected checks and the production receipt bind the final main SHA.
requirements.falsifier: Runtime/release-shell content changes after preview, required checks fail, approval parity fails, the merge omits the exact preview ancestor, or production lacks a matching source/Pages receipt and live smoke.

evidence.note: GitHub Actions artifact 8622616687 was created from the exact clean runtime SHA before release authorization was recorded.
The acceptance gate enforces complete coverage, preview-to-approval ordering and no post-preview runtime or release-shell drift.
The exact two-channel candidate is served through chooser, Stable, latest, normal and room routes.
